scope: Covers the work on integrate/monday-pilot: the zero-DNS send profile merged from feat/zero-dns-send-profile, the do-not-contact subdomain fix, the BC-01 spec and test rewrite from staff ACCESS isolation to workspace DATA isolation, the CI test-evidence recorder, and the CLASSIFY/DOMAIN records. It does NOT cover anything already live on production (b36e66e), and it does NOT cover the Customer-Ready condition of the deployed product, which is graded separately and is below the sell gate.

architect.design_note: No new architecture. Two behaviour changes, both narrowing: (1) a hosted unsubscribe URL may now be minted ONLY on a client-aligned link domain, with the app-domain fallback removed from the module entirely so it cannot return by accident, falling through to a mailto rail on the sending mailbox; (2) domain suppression now matches the recipient domain OR any of its parents, splitting on label boundaries so lookalikes still do not match. Both make the system refuse more, never send more. The BC-01 rewrite changed no code: it corrected a spec that asserted a property the product deliberately does not have.

test.output: Measured on integrate/monday-pilot, 2026-08-23, machine-readable output recorded in .bidlow/EVIDENCE.json. npm run lint -> exit 0. npm run typecheck -> exit 0. npm test -> 1875 passed / 1875 total across 216 files, exit 0. npm run build -> exit 0 (webpack production build, route table emitted). npm run test:e2e -> 15 passed / 0 failed / 0 flaky, exit 0, including the rewritten 6-test BC-01 workspace data-isolation suite.
test.gap: The BC-01 tests did NOT go red first, because the data boundary already held: the send path carries loader scoping plus four clientId guards in sequence-send-policy.ts that were already unit-tested, and the read paths were already clientId-scoped. They were instead PROVEN capable of failing: on a scratch branch, removing the clientId scope from the outbound query in src/server/activity/client-activity.ts turned R-5 red, with Client B's activity disclosing Client A's prospect address. Reverted. Only R-5 was proven this way; R-1, R-6 and E-03 guard different mechanisms and their discriminating power is asserted from reading, not proven by breakage. Also NOT covered: the mailbox-shared-between-two-workspaces hole recorded as E-06, which no test exercises.

security.findings: Cross-workspace DATA isolation verified live against a production build: per-client activity is scoped (Client A shows its prospect and subject, Client B shows neither); replies never cross because no InboundReply is created without a matching outbound in the same client; suppression is per-client by construction. Cross-staff ACCESS isolation is ABSENT BY DESIGN and is now recorded as a decision with three reversal triggers, not as a gap. The unsubscribe change removes a live cross-domain link that was the confirmed cause of a quarantine. The suppression change widens what is blocked and cannot cause a send.
security.not_reviewed: E-06: the same mailbox address may be connected to two workspaces, and each then stores its own copy of every raw inbound message including full bodyText. Recorded in the spec, not fixed and not tested. Also unreviewed: the API surface as distinct from the pages (export, search, reports), named in the spec as the classic forgotten-permission gap.

sre.pipeline: CI now records test evidence in both jobs from the runners' own machine-readable output and uploads it as an artifact, with if: always() so a RED run leaves a record saying so. This closed a real gap: the ship gate reads .bidlow/EVIDENCE.json and nothing in the repo was writing it, so the gate's central assumption was false and it blocked every push with no route forward.
sre.note: Nothing is deployed by this chain. Branch protection means Greg merges, and deploy-production.yml runs prisma migrate deploy against the production database BEFORE the Azure login step -- so a deploy that dies at login has already migrated production. This branch carries NO schema change and NO migration, deliberately: the DNC related-domain setting was kept out of it for exactly that reason.

reviewer.attempted_refutations: Tried to break the BC-01 rewrite and failed to: the positive control initially failed on toBeVisible, which turned out to be correct behaviour (the activity feed sits in a collapsed <details>) and led to asserting DOM presence instead -- the stricter property, since data delivered to another workspace's browser is disclosed whether or not CSS paints it. Tried to confirm the 0% bounce rate was explained by a disabled flag and REFUTED it: MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED is true in production, so the earlier inference was withdrawn. Tried to confirm E-02 (a staff user with no membership sees nothing) and REFUTED it live: such a user sees every workspace.
reviewer.blocking_gaps_recorded: Customer-Ready is 4 and the product is below the sell gate. The 4.0 cap was applied for the app-domain unsubscribe link, which THIS branch fixes -- but the grade describes the DEPLOYED product, and production still serves b36e66e. The grade cannot honestly move until this ships and is re-walked. Uncapped it was 6.0, still below 8. Also outstanding: Art.28 DPAs unverified with Sentry, RocketReach and Resend.

head_of_engineering.reason: Signed for the ENGINEERING work on this branch only, on evidence, by the agent playing the role -- not by a second human. Every gate was run and its real output recorded: lint 0, typecheck 0, 1875/1875 unit across 216 files, 15/15 e2e, build green, all captured programmatically in EVIDENCE.json rather than asserted. The two behaviour changes both narrow what the system will send. The BC-01 rewrite was authorised by Greg in writing and the freeze amended in his name.
head_of_engineering.evidence: .bidlow/EVIDENCE.json (machine-derived from vitest and playwright JSON reporters, this commit). Live verification against a production build for the data boundary and the Azure App Service settings read for MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED=true, MAILBOX_COMPLAINT_DETECTION_ENABLED=true, MAILBOX_WARMUP_RAMP=on, OPEN_TRACKING_PIXEL=off.
head_of_engineering.what_would_unblock: This sign-off does NOT clear the Tier P sell gate and must not be read as doing so. Customer-Ready is 4 (uncapped 6), below 8, so the product may not be sold. What moves it: ship this branch, then re-walk production as a customer and re-grade -- the specific defect behind the 4.0 cap is fixed in this code but is still live on b36e66e.
